meta.notes: Torah #202 has zero bechina edges in the dataset (reference===202 does not appear in torahData.js at all). The source text (torah_202.txt) is a single-sentence teaching stating: anyone whose intellect (sekhel) is very small needs to be given very much honor, because the smaller one's intellect, the more one desires honor — proven empirically by the observation that women, whose da'at is light and small, are very exacting about their honor. The teaching contains no bechina language whatsoever (no בְּחִינַת, no הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, no נִקְרָא, no הוּא בְּחִינַת). The sole structural relationship is a causal/inverse correlation: small sekhel → great desire for kavod. This is an eitza relationship (cause-and-effect / directional), not a bechina (parallel aspects / shared essence). The mention of da'at as the explanation for sekhel's smallness does not constitute a formal bechina equation — the Rebbe uses da'at and sekhel interchangeably in context, but no explicit bechina identification is made between them. Without any bechina edges, no connected components can be formed, and therefore no packages can be proposed.
